text:
Alice Park: Quick sync — we need to lock a prioritization for the dedicated-capacity allocation work this sprint. Customers (big SaaS X + payment platform Y) are asking for per-route guarantees and finer quota slabs. Do we do: (A) per-route reserved throughput, (B) more granular per-tenant quota slabs, or (C) a larger shared burst buffer with reactive autoscale? :thinking:

Miguel Santos: +1 on making this explicit. data question: what's the delta in infra cost between (B) and (C)? rough ballpark ok.

Priya Nair: From SRE side, (C) is easiest to operate initially — single global burst pool reduces fragmentation. But it complicates fairness and billing reconciliation.

Tom Becker: Billing/PMI note: (A) requires changes to metering (per-route counters) and UI to let customers opt-in. That's 2-3 sprints for telemetry + exports.

Jenna Li: Customer success — customers asking for per-route because they have mixed workloads (low-latency chat + high-throughput embeddings). They'd pay premium for per-route guarantees.

Alice Park: Proposal: split into two deliverables. 1) Minimum Viable Guarantees (MVP): per-tenant quota slabs + burst buffer with simple priority tiers. 2) Follow-up: per-route reserved throughput (opt-in) + metering + billing. Thoughts?

Miguel Santos: Sounds pragmatic. Need concrete launch criteria for MVP. Suggest: latency P50/P95 within SLA for premium tenants under 2x baseline load, and <5% tail amplification from bursting.

Priya Nair: Ops checklist for MVP:
- admission control enforcement implemented
- observability: per-tenant token-level latency + burst usage dashboards
- rollout gating: canary on 3 customers then region-wide

Tom Becker: Billing side checklist:
- quota slabs defined and synced to billing DB
- overage export + alerting
- currency implications for multi-region customers

Alice Park: add acceptance criteria:
- Performance: 99% of requests for premium tenants meet configured latency SLO at target load window
- Cost: infra delta <= 15% for customers on standard plan (we'll present tradeoffs to sales)
- Audit: KMS/logs for quota decisions in Private deployments

Jenna Li: Customer comms draft snippet: "We are launching quota slabs + burst buffer to reduce application-level throttling. Per-route reservations are coming later for customers needing strict isolation."

Miguel Santos: Technical concern: shared burst buffer needs eviction preemption rules. Suggest simple priority preempt: premium > standard > best-effort and configurable preempt window.

Priya Nair: Agreed. Also add an emergency fallback where autoscale can preempt pooled burst and spin up conservative capacity for safety-critical tenants.

Alice Park: ok, assign owners: Miguel -> runtime changes (burst buffer + preempt), Priya -> rollout + observability, Tom -> billing + metering, Jenna -> customer comms + pilot coordination. I'll own product/PR.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: branch dedicated/alloc-mvp -> staging (CI #4827)

Tom Becker: One more: we should surface "quota usage forecast" in console so customers can self-serve to avoid surprise throttles. Low effort: show 7-day burn rate + projected exhaustion.

Miguel Santos: add to scope if we have bandwidth. Otherwise mark as "console follow-up".

Alice Park: Decision: scope MVP = per-tenant quota slabs + shared burst buffer + priority preemption + rollout gating + console forecast as follow-up. Per-route reservations moved to Q2 after pilot results. Launch criteria tracked in the feature checklist doc. :+1:

Jenna Li: I'll start recruiting pilot customers (X, Y, Z) and draft the pilot success metrics (95% of premium route requests under SLO during simulated surge).

Priya Nair: I'll prepare canary plan + playbook with rollback triggers (errors > 3% or tail latency increase > 30% within canary window).

Alice Park: Thanks all. Next sync Thurs 10am to review pilot readiness. If anyone hits a blocker, @here bring it up in this thread.
